title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This is the last page (93 of 93) of the June 1986 notes. It finishes a check begun on p. 92. The setting is an axiomatic 'analysis situs' framework. There is a category F of 'spaces/objects' with distinguished subsets L ('linear'/elementary objects) and M. There is a relation x ≪ X ('x is well inside / way-below X'), and a strict version x ˚≪ X meaning x ∈ voisb(X), i.e. x lies in a neighbourhood-type class of X. Axioms are numbered Ax/At 8, 9, 10, 11, 11 bis, 12, 13, 14, 14 bis.

On p. 92 Grothendieck takes a (full) subcategory F' ⊂ F and sets L' = L ∩ F' and M' = M ∩ F'. He imposes conditions labelled Sous-cat 3, 3' and 4:
- Sous-cat 3 ('épaisse', thick for the bounds): if X ∈ M', x ∈ L and x ≪ X, then x ∈ F'.
- Sous-cat 3' ('assez dense'): every X ∈ M' admits some x ∈ L ∩ F' with x ˚≪ X.
- Sous-cat 4: if X, Y ∈ M' satisfy the relation X‖Y in F, then the same relation holds in F'.
He notes that 3 implies 3', that both imply Ax 8 for F', and that Ax 9 is not automatically inherited by subcategories, even full ones.

This page completes the inheritance table:
- Ax 9: under Sous-cat 3 (for a full subcategory) together with Sous-cat 4, Ax 9 for F gives Ax 9 for F'.
- Ax 10 (or Ax 11): given Sous-cat 4 and Sous-cat 3, the axiom for F' implies the same for F. The machine transcription gives the direction F' ⇒ F; it is hard to confirm from the image.
- Ax 11 bis and Ax 12: these become a stability property of F' inside F.
- Ax 13: under Sous-cat 3 and 4, validity in F implies validity in F'.
- Ax 14: automatic.
- Ax 14 bis: follows from a stability condition.

The page then ends with a closing rule. So the purpose is purely to check which axioms of the abstract framework pass to suitable full subcategories ('sous-catégories épaisses'). Presumably this is so that the framework can be restricted, e.g. to tame or polyhedral subclasses.
errors: Not really checkable: the axioms At 9–14 bis are defined on earlier pages not provided. The direction 'At 10 pour F' implique idem pour F' looks odd (one would expect F ⇒ F' as for At 9 and At 13). It may be a slip or a transcription ambiguity, and it is unverifiable here.

ideas.what: A 'thick' (épaisse) subcategory for a way-below/neighbourhood relation: closed under passing to smaller elementary objects x ≪ X. Plus an 'assez dense' variant requiring cofinal elementary neighbourhoods.
ideas.modern_name: Downward-closed / cofinal subclasses with respect to a way-below or compact-containment relation (cf. bases in domain theory, cofinality conditions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: General order-theoretic folklore; not a specific named result
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to the 'tame topology' programme sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but this specific axiomatics is not published to my knowledge

ideas.what: Inheritance table of the axioms (Ax 9–14 bis) under passage to full subcategories satisfying Sous-cat 3/4.
ideas.modern_name: Stability of axiomatic structure under restriction to full subcategories

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a short closing bookkeeping check of which axioms of an unpublished abstract 'analysis situs' framework descend to thick or dense full subcategories. The surrounding axiomatics may be of historical interest as an unpublished 1986 attempt at tame-topology foundations. But this page itself contains no substantive new construction or connection.
transcription_corrections: 'aux Énoncés 3' should likely read 'aux Sous-cat 3' (the same abbreviation as 'Sous-cat 3/4' on p. 92); likewise 'Énoncé 4' → 'Sous-cat 4' and 'Énoncé 3' → 'Sous-cat 3' throughout.
'(cohésion pleine)' is more plausibly '(catégorie pleine)', referring to a full subcategory.
'il est question de lisses' is doubtful; it may be 'il soit question de liens' or a similar phrase. Illegible, best marked [?].
'At' is presumably the same as 'Ax' (axiome) used on p. 92.
Line 'At 11 bis ... automatique' plausibly reads 'At 11 bis pour F' est une propriété de stabilité de F' dans F (résultant automatiquement?)'.
